name: gpu_path_trace

libraries.name: Embree
libraries.usage: Builds the BVH2 (rtcBuildBVH, SAH) that the compute traversal path walks on GPUs without ray query support, before the measurement starts. The ray query and Metal paths do not use it.
libraries.notes: Built as a static library from the pinned submodule with the internal tasking system, triangle geometry only and runtime ISA dispatch; no source modifications. arm64 builds include Embree's vendored SSE2NEON header (MIT).

libraries.name: cgltf
libraries.usage: Parses the glTF models of the bundled scene before the measurement starts.
libraries.notes: Single header library compiled into the task from the pinned submodule; no source modifications.

libraries.name: nlohmann/json
libraries.usage: Parses the scene description (scene.json) before the measurement starts.
libraries.notes: Header only library compiled into the task from the pinned submodule; no source modifications.

libraries.name: stb
libraries.usage: Decodes the scene textures (JPEG) and the HDR environment map before the measurement, and encodes the rendered frame as PNG afterwards.
libraries.notes: Single header libraries compiled into the task from the pinned submodule; no source modifications.

libraries.name: Poly Haven scene assets
libraries.usage: The bundled models and HDR environment (common/assets/raytrace_scene/) that make up the rendered scene.
libraries.notes: Seven models and one HDRI, unmodified, shared with cpu_raytrace; the arrangement in scene.json is part of the task.

title: GPU ray traced rendering
short_description: Path traced render of a bundled scene on the graphics processor.

structured_text.description: Renders a bundled scene with a path tracer that runs on the graphics processor, tracing rays and accumulating samples toward a clean image. The scene, sample budget and resolution are fixed, and the work uses the GPU's ray tracing and compute paths together.
structured_text.metric_explanation: The score is the average number of accumulated frames produced per second, reported in fps, which scales with how quickly the image converges.
structured_text.value_interpretation: Higher is better. A higher rate means faster previews and shorter final renders when working with ray traced lighting.
structured_text.reasoning: GPU path tracing is now central to high end content creation and to ray traced game effects, and it stresses both ray traversal and shading on the GPU.
